dedupe_keys.name: sereway security and reliability benchmarking testbed for the railway industrial internet of things

description: SereWay is an open-source testbed for benchmarking how well machine learning tools detect security and reliability anomalies in the railway Industrial Internet of Things. It was published in 2026 in the Journal of Network and Systems Management by Alessandra Rizzardi, Raffaele Della Corte and co-authors from the University of Insubria and the University of Naples Federico II. The testbed builds on Open-fari, an existing railway anomaly detection testbed, and uses lightweight virtualisation with synthetic data generators trained on real train sensor data to create normal and faulty system behaviour, while distributed denial of service attacks come from a botnet simulation framework. The authors used it in an experimental campaign to evaluate a federated learning system that detects both security and reliability anomalies, and report that it can emulate realistic railway scenarios. Coverage: generic onboard and wayside railway IoT systems. Access: described in an open-access article as open source; the code location and licence were not confirmed during this pass. Licence and cost: free; the article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: synthetic data and emulated attacks, limited attack types, and a research prototype. It supports digital twin style experiments and studies of cyber and fault cascades in railway systems. It complements the Electra traction substation ICS dataset in the catalogue.
